newsitem.title: USA: NationsBank unit wins NASD arbitration case.
newsitem.headline: NationsBank unit wins NASD arbitration case.

text.p: NationsSecurities, the brokerage unit of NationsBank Corp, said Thursday that an arbitration panel of the National Association of Securities Dealers has dismissed claims by three of its former brokers of improper sales practices they alleged were in effect in 1994.
NationsSecurities said the panel rejected all requests by the three former brokers, who worked for the brokerage in Florida in 1993 and 1994, for damages, back pay, expenses or attorneys fees.

It said the panel unanimously decided the former brokers were not fired or retaliated against for "blowing the whistle" on wrongful sales practices. NationsSecurities said that during hearings of the case in Tampa, it denied all allegations of improper sales practices and the panel concluded that the brokerage has no liability.

NationsSecurities said that while the arbitrators found that none of the former brokers was fired or retaliated against, they felt that one of the three -- David A. Cray -- may have been "confused" and directed NationsSecurities to offer him his old job, without back pay or benefits.
The two other former brokers in the case are Robert Lewis and Catherine Hovis, NationsSecurities said.
The three could not be reached for comment.
